PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

According to recent reports, feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

“In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”.

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

Goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

According to recent reports, fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

ADO Den Haag 3-1 Sparta Rotterdam.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 2-5 PSV Eindhoven.

Breaking: Record-breaking Harry Kane belongs in the company of greats that he keeps. There is only one gap in his record now and he remains as central to ending 60 years of hurt than he has ever been, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:17 EST, 12 November 2026.
  • Only giants have trodden the path that Harry Kane walked at Wembley on Thursday when he strode out on to the pitch on a bitterly cold winter night, his four young children by his side, and beheld the array of trophies, honours, adulation and respect that awaited him.
  • It is just 16 days since Kane held his hands to his face, climbed up to the stage at the London Palladium and said 'wow' when Ronaldo 'Il Fenomeno' presented him with the Ballon d'Or trophy that anointed him the best player in the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:17 EST, 12 November 2026.

Only giants have trodden the path that Harry Kane walked at Wembley on Thursday when he strode out on to the pitch on a bitterly cold winter night, his four young children by his side, and beheld the array of trophies, honours, adulation and respect that awaited him.

It is just 16 days since Kane held his hands to his face, climbed up to the stage at the London Palladium and said 'wow' when Ronaldo 'Il Fenomeno' presented him with the Ballon d'Or trophy that anointed him the best player in the world.

Now, it sat before him on a plinth and Kane broke away from the England line-up and walked forward to hoist it aloft. He revealed it to all the corners of the stadium and for a moment, it was framed against the giant tifo bearing his image and the words 'England's Finest' that towered over one end of the ground.

In a recent development, but the Ballon d’Or is old news in the flood of honours that is coming Kane’s way in this golden summer of a great career. Kane had become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or for a quarter of a century and on Thursday night he was to break the 37-year-old record held by Peter Shilton for the most England caps. He scored the winner, too. Of course, he did.

According to recent reports, the occasion of England-Croatia in the Nations League was Kane's 126th appearance in an England shirt and Shilton stepped forward to hand him a small case containing a crest to mark the achievement. Finally, the Prince of Wales demonstrated his appreciation to the England captain by presenting him with a commemorative shirt with 'Kane 126' emblazoned on it.

Sources indicate that it was a night to feel the weight of football's history and the ghosts of greatness that people England's heritage. Kane belongs in the manufacturer he now keeps. He belongs in the pantheon of the game because he is one of the deadliest strikers in history. He belongs in the pantheon because of the humility he has shown and the dedication he devotes to improvement.

Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking England appearance with a finely struck penalty.

Before kick-off, Kane's history-making was celebrated with a commemorative shirt by the Prince of Wales.

England (4-2-3-1): Pickford 6; Alexander-Arnold 6 (White 78, 6), Quansah 4, Burn 6, Hall 7; Rice 5 (Garner 78, 5), Anderson 6; Rogers 8, Bellingham 6, Gordon 5 (Ngumoha 78, 5); Kane 7.

Goals: Rogers 24', Kane 64' (pen).

Croatia (4-2-3-1): Livakovic 5; Smolcic 6 (Marco Pasalic 76 5), Stanisic 6, Vuskovic 6, Gvardiol 5; Misic 5 (Modric 76, 6), Kovacic 6; Sucic 7 (Mario Pasalic 70, 5), Baturina 6, Vlasic 5; Matanovic 5 (Budimir 70, 5).

In a recent development, he belongs with Billy Wright, the first England player to 100 caps, and the man who set the England appearance record at 105 when he played for his country for the last time in 1959. He belongs with Bobby Charlton, who made it to 106 before the heartbreak of the 1970 World Cup quarter-final defeat to West Germany brought his international career to an end.

Recent findings suggest that kane belongs with Bobby Moore, Charlton's rival as the greatest England player of all time, who reached the latest mark of 108 caps in November 1973. That was one of the great numbers in English sport until Peter Shilton finally surpassed it. He reached 125 caps by the time he played his last game for England in the third-place play-off at the 1990 World Cup.

Industry observers note that it is quite some lineage. And now it is Kane who holds the prize. And if this was hardly a momentous match, it was a momentous occasion. If you are tired of glorying in a player like Kane, a relentless striker, a wonderful passer, the sweetest striker of the ball you will ever see, a player of vision, a man who exudes the beauty of simplicity and the wonder of modesty, then you are tired of football.

The honours are rushing at him in a giddy, babbling flood. It may be that he reaches close to 200 caps before he retires and even if it already seems likely that that record will be broken by Jude Bellingham, who has 61 caps at the age of 23, Kane's England goals tally, which stands at 92 after another goal against Croatia, will not be under threat for a generation or longer.

Recent findings suggest that the gap, of course, is a tournament victory. That is what still separates Moore and Charlton from him. Kane is a dream of a player but he has not won the World Cup or the European Championship. What remains is the hope that he will put that right in the years that he has left in the game.

Industry observers note that winning the Nations League would not be quite the same but it would be a start and this victory over Croatia took England a small step closer to that goal. A convincing win over Spain in Madrid on Sunday would take them closer to their aim of finishing top of this group and getting a favourable draw in the quarter-finals in the spring.

Kane made his England debut in March 2015 when he was 21 and England's future looks brighter now than it did when he broke through. More than an hour before the game, the men who will follow Kane and perhaps even chase his caps record, chatted animatedly on the pitch. Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Gibbs-White are the new breed.

Morgan Rogers opened the scoring inside the opening half-an-hour and celebrated with his trademark cold celebration.

England had found themselves pegged back by Croatia after slopping defending drew the visitors level.

Referee Morten Krogh was summoned to the monitor to review the penalty shout on Thursday.

Kane returned to Wembley triumphant for the first time since his historic Ballon d'Or win.

Recent findings suggest that after the Kane festivities, the first half was an anti-climax. Twenty-four minutes of relative drudgery ensued before Kane exhibited the breadth of his talent once again to help put England ahead. He got the ball 30 yards out, looked up and drifted a beautiful diagonal pass out to the right and into the path of Bellingham. Bellingham volleyed it across goal and Rogers forced it over the line.

The second half began slowly, too, but 15 minutes into it, Croatia equalised. England failed to clear a corner, Jarell Quansah tried to head the ball back to Jordan Pickford and, as Kane watched on, Petar Sucic stole in and hooked the ball past the England goalkeeper into the roof of the net.

Recent findings suggest that quansah made some kind of amends three minutes later when he was dragged down in the box and Danish referee Morten Krogh awarded a penalty. It was Kane-time again. Kane took the kick and lifted it gently and with a touch of curl down the centre of the goal. Dominic Livakovic dived to his left and the ball sailed softly over his trailing leg and into the net.

According to recent reports, croatia had chances to draw level but could not take them. England made changes and young Rio Ngumoha, a winger of rare talent, another with a rich future ahead of him, another who will help to fill the void when the day comes for Kane to bid farewell to England, came on as a late substitute for Gordon.

And so Kane's night of history began to draw to a close. In a 2-1 victory, he had made one and scored one. He remains as central to England's hopes of ending more than 60 years without a trophy as he ever has been. In a career that has festooned him with garlands and left no one in doubt of his greatness, it is the only gap that remains.

Harry Kane has set his sights firmly on rapidly reaching a century of international goals after becoming England’s most-capped player of all time.

The England skipper marked his 126th appearance for the Three Lions with the winner against Croatia in the Nations League – his first goal since picking up the Ballon d’Or last month.

Kane was afforded an emotional presentation pre-match at Wembley to mark both achievements and is already thinking of creating more history after moving within eight goals of a ton.

‘It’s achievable,’ Kane remarked. ‘I’m getting closer. Breaking the appearance record is a massive thing in the history of our game, seeing the tifo at the stadium and having my kids with me was beyond dreams.

‘It’s crucial to recognise our great players. It’s maybe something we haven’t done so well over the years with some of our other greats.

‘It's been a crazy few weeks. I don’t know if I’ve fully taken it all in. The reception has been overwhelming.

‘Maybe during the winter break I’ll be on a beach reflecting on everything I’ve achieved, having a drink with my wife.’.

Croatia legend Luka Modric, 41, was part of the presentations ahead of kick off and Kane did not rule out attempting to prolong his career in a similar vein to the AC Milan midfielder.

‘He’s an inspiration for a lot of us,’ Kane added. ‘An incredible player and a great person, he’s looked after himself and still to be playing at this level is inspiring for me to push the limits. To see where your body and mentality takes you.

According to recent reports, ‘As long as I feel I can help, I’ll be here for as long as I can. If that’s until I’m 40, we’ll wait and see.’.

Now qualified for the quarter-finals, England need to beat Spain in Madrid on Sunday to top their group and Thomas Tuchel believes they can topple the world champions.

It has been revealed that ‘It’s a completely different scenario, completely different setup,’ Tuchel mentioned. ‘But I'm very positive that we will get what we want.’.

Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s upcoming era lift-off

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5146 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his fresh kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.
  • Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.
  • Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his fresh kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this upcoming Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

It has been revealed that jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0.

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

In a recent development, mcGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo.

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Sources indicate that emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”.

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Sources indicate that vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim.

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1.

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s newly introduced goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Industry observers note that jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu.

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7.

It has been revealed that villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

It has been revealed that slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

In a recent development, really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

According to recent reports, barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A massive let-off for Villa.

Industry observers note that gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Abraham replaces goalscorer Jackson.

It has been revealed that villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Sources indicate that lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

It has been revealed that brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Industry observers note that the Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [significant] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a upcoming test.”.

It has been revealed that the experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a fresh-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s fresh-look crew.

Recent findings suggest that morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his latest recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Sources indicate that although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

Recent findings suggest that cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is at the moment playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

In a recent development, his son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.

  • J'ai vraiment pris conscience que quelque chose avait changé lors de nos déplacements en championnat après Kiev.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Après le carton de son livre Foot Sentimental paru il y a 3 ans aux éditions Le Cherche midi, Dominique Rocheteau a fait paraître le mois dernier dans la même maison Soif d'Idéal. L'Ange Vert revient dans ce bouquin - anecdotes à l'appui - sur la Rocheteaumania qui a envahi la France après le mythique quart de finale retour de Coupe d'Europe des Clubs Champions qui s'est déroulé le 17 mars 1976 dans le Chaudron. Extraits.

Recent findings suggest that "C'est seulement le lendemain de notre victoire contre Kiev, puis dans les jours qui ont suivi, que j'ai commencé à prendre la mesure de ce qui venait de se passer. Peu à peu, j'ai perçu l'ampleur de cette vague verte qui n'allait cesser de grandir, et de ce que ce match allait changer dans ma vie. À l'entraînement, une foule que je n'avais encore jamais vue pour un simple décrassage nous attendait : à l'entrée, à la sortie, tout autour du terrain. Que du vert. Cette fois, j'ai pu saluer mes parents à la sortie du stade, juste avant qu'ils ne reprennent la route. J’étais heureux, bien sûr, mais je l'avoue un peu perdu, déconcerté, face à cet engouement auquel je n'étais absolument pas préparé.

J'ai vraiment pris conscience que quelque chose avait changé lors de nos déplacements en championnat après Kiev. C'était comme si toute la France était derrière nous. Et puis, il y avait les médias, plus seulement sportifs : Paris Match, Télé 7 Jours, Rock & Folk, Rolling Stones, Salut les copains, Pif Gadget… Je ne lisais pas les journaux, je ne regardais pas la télévision. J'étais un peu dans mon monde, mais désormais je devais « apprendre » à me raconter. J'acceptais les demandes, plus par politesse que par réelle envie. Je me retrouvais souvent pris de court, parfois même paniqué. Je n'avais pas d'agent. Les journalistes passaient par le club pour leurs demandes d'interview, et je me sentais obligé d'accepter. À 20 ans, je ne contrôlais rien. Un jour, je me suis rendu compte que j'avais donné une interview pour un magazine érotique… quand ils m'ont envoyé le numéro. C'est aussi après Kiev que l'on a commencé à m'appeler l’« Ange vert », un surnom que j'ai mis du temps à apprécier.

Ce qui m'a le plus désarçonné, ce sont ces sacs de courriers qui ont commencé à arriver. Que faire de tout ça ? Je lisais quelques lettres, mais il y en avait des milliers. Il y avait de tout : des demandes en mariage, des déclarations d'amour, des confidences, des photos, des messages, comme si nous nous connaissions depuis toujours. Après les vacances d'été et celles de Noël, quand je revenais de Charente-Maritime, le secrétaire de l'AS Saint-Étienne m'invitait à passer récupérer au stade des sacs postaux. « Il y en a plusieurs kilos ». Je devinais à son ton que cela représentait une charge de travail. Ils étaient remplis de lettres et parfois de cassettes audio de filles envoyant des compliments ou des messages, par exemple : « Dominique, j'aimerais bien que l'on se voit ». Certaines glissaient même un chewing-gum à l'intérieur. Beaucoup de lettres venaient de filles. Certaines m'avouaient qu'elles m'aimaient.

Il y avait aussi des plaisanteries comme cette lettre émanant de lycéennes d'un établissement religieux en région parisienne qui suggérait mon mariage avec une fille « de bonne famille » de leur entourage. D'autres donnaient des recettes miracles pour faire cesser les rhumes ou bien améliorer le tonus. Des collégiens racontaient aussi le plaisir qu'ils avaient à chanter pendant leurs cours la chanson « Allez les Verts » pour embêter leurs professeurs. Beaucoup de lettres venaient d'Afrique, où Saint-Étienne était très aimé. Certaines étaient longues, parfois plusieurs pages et vraiment très belles. Mais aussi des pays de l'Est -Pologne, Allemagne de l'Est, Tchécoslovaquie - d'où de nombreux collectionneurs m'envoyaient des photos parues dans les magazines afin que je les signe. J'en reçois encore aujourd'hui au siège du club qui me les fait suivre à chaque fois.

Mes amis Hugues et Louis - qui habitait à Saint-Héand et préparait son concours du barreau - et moi, nous nous asseyions par terre dans la salle à manger pour trier le courrier. Impossible de répondre à tout le monde. Nous envoyions une photo dédicacée à ceux qui avaient joint une enveloppe timbrée à leur nom. Certains glissaient même un billet de 20 ou 50 francs pour recevoir une photo signée. Nous remettions ensuite les enveloppes à la postière de Saint-Héand qui nous félicitait : « Joli travail ! », avant de les oblitérer. À travers toutes ces petites histoires, j'étais à la fois touché mais aussi terriblement gêné. Tout cela me paraissait énorme, démesuré. Dans la rue, j'appréciais les marques de sympathie même si elles me mettaient mal à l'aise. Je ne savais pas toujours quoi dire, alors je répondais par un sourire.

Un matin de juillet 1976, j'étais en vacances chez mes parents. Je dormais encore tandis que ma mère et Louis prenaient le café dans le jardin. Un jeune homme s'est présenté derrière le grillage et a demandé à me voir. Ma mère lui a demandé s'il me connaissait. Devant sa réponse affirmative et son insistance, elle a fini par le laisser entrer. Ils sont venus me réveiller. « Il y a un ami qui veut te voir ». Je me suis levé, surpris. « Je ne vous connais pas » -  « Si, je vous ai vu à un match »… « Qu'est-ce que vous voulez ? » « Un autographe ». Je me suis exécuté et il est reparti ravi. Je suis resté partagé entre la satisfaction de faire plaisir et le malaise de voir ma vie privée ainsi envahie.

Une autre fois, peu après avoir fait construire mon chalet à La Gimont, je suis rentré de l'entraînement et j'ai constaté que mon chat, Diamant, avait disparu. Une femme était venue chez moi, l'avait emmenée et avait fait savoir à mon entourage que si je voulais le récupérer, je devais me rendre personnellement chez elle à Veauche, à une dizaine de kilomètres. Mon ami Louis a tenté de la raisonner, en vain. Que faire ? Il n'était pas question pour moi de céder à ce chantage. Je ne voulais pas y aller, mais je tenais à récupérer mon chat. Yves, le frère de Louis, a alors appelé la gendarmerie de Saint-Galmier. Les gendarmes se sont rendus à Veauche et ont réussi à convaincre la dame de rendre Diamant. Ils n'ont toutefois pas pu le ramener eux-mêmes. Sur leur conseil, Louis a sauté dans sa voiture pour aller le chercher. Quand il est arrivé, le chat était couché sur un coussin, sur une chaise. La femme lui a lancé : « Voyez, il avait déjà pris ses marques. » Grâce à Louis et à l'intervention des gendarmes, j'ai pu récupérer Diamant et une fois de plus mesurer la chance que j'avais d'avoir des amis en or. 1976 a été une année folle. Depuis Kiev, tout avait changé autour de moi, mais je n'ai jamais vraiment cherché à me protéger ni à mettre de la distance entre moi et les autres. Je voulais simplement vivre une vie normale, comme les autres jeunes de mon époque.".

Dutch progress in Nations League despite 5-0 drubbing in Germany

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

But in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

Sources indicate that dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La retraite internationale de Romelu Lukaku (33 ans), meilleur buteur de l'histoire en sélection belge (94 pions en 135 sélections), laisse un grand vide chez les Diables Rouges. Comme l'a souligné hier La Dernière Heure Les Sports +, les candidats ne manquent pas mais le Diablotin Lucas Stassin part de loin. Extraits.

Sources indicate that "Charles De Ketelaere a pris le relais, dans un autre style mais sans être remis en question. Il est le titulaire incontesté en pointe, même s'il joue à une autre position à l'Atalanta. Il sera d'ailleurs intéressant de voir s'il osera prendre le n°9 au prochain rassemblement. Qui pour doubler CDK dorénavant ? Le casting est large et étonnamment ouvert.

According to recent reports, loïs Openda peut y penser, lui qui retrouvait peu à peu ses sensations à Lyon avant de se blesser et de manquer ce rassemblement. Mais parviendra-t-il enfin à éclore en équipe nationale alors qu'il fêtera bientôt son 27e anniversaire ? Il n'a inscrit que trois buts chez les Diables jusqu'à présent.

Industry observers note that hugo Cuypers, le Belge le plus prolifique ces derniers mois, peut espérer monter en grade après avoir fêté sa première sélection. Mais lui aura 30 ans au prochain rassemblement. Il ne sera pas une solution à long terme et devra aussi prouver qu'il peut avoir le niveau en évoluant dans le championnat mexicain.

L'avant-centre le plus prometteur en Belgique, c'est probablement Matias Fernandez-Pardo (21 ans), mais avec un tout autre profil que Lukaku et De Ketelaere. Acheté 60 M€ par Newcastle cet été, il possède une vitesse et une puissance de jambes assez phénoménales. Le tout avec un vrai sens du but.

Le sélectionneur a aussi une autre option, très différente : le faux 9. Deux joueurs sont capables de prendre ce rôle, que CDK peut parfois avoir selon le moment du match. On pense à Leandro Trossard, qui avait par moments dépanné Arsenal devant, et à Mika Godts, barré sur les flancs par Jeremy Doku et Diego Moreira. Lui aussi a déjà évolué en faux 9, à l'Ajax.

L'idée sera aussi de regarder dans le réservoir belge. En Espoirs, trois attaquants prouvent qu'ils ont des qualités : Lucas Stassin, Romeo Vermant et Norman Bassette. À tel point que le coach Gill Swerts a cherché un système pour en utiliser au moins deux des trois en même temps. Leur évolution en club fera beaucoup de leur avenir à court terme chez les Diables.".

Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
  • According to recent reports, he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

According to recent reports, he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he noted.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Recent findings suggest that given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

In a recent development, that was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a upcoming manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

Playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

In a recent development, there were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

In a recent development, millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

According to recent reports, millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

Newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

So much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

According to recent reports, well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil said: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

“We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

It has been revealed that as for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

Sources indicate that the draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

Recent findings suggest that the third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” said Willock after the match.

Sources indicate that “100% [the competition is key], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a upcoming coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a big game in keeping that momentum.”.

"We remarked at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

Industry observers note that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

In a recent development, newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

In a recent development, finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

In a recent development, marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Sources indicate that double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

Free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

What colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

According to recent reports, newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

Millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

Industry observers note that the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

The delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Industry observers note that newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

González is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

According to recent reports, millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Industry observers note that newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

In a recent development, first piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Industry observers note that barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

In a recent development, wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

Newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Recent findings suggest that another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Sources indicate that murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

According to recent reports, fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Just a reminder of the teams starting today:.

Starting XI: Filip Marschall; Jordi Osei-Tutu, Caleb Taylor, Jake Cooper, Elkan Baggott; Lyndon Dykes, Jenson Metcalfe; Camiel Neghli, Daniel Kelly, Romain Esse; Zak Lovelace.

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge.

Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa.

Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur.

Sources indicate that the teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

"We've tried to find the right balance" ⚖️Matthias Jaissle on his team selection for tonight's match with Millwall ⚫️ pic.twitter.com/kiRRxAgLk8.

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

Alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach indicates has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

According to recent reports, at the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

You can read Luke Edwards’ full story on that here.

The Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:.

Peterborough United vs Barnsley (7.45pm).

Fleetwood Town vs Sheffield United (7.45pm).

Manchester City vs Norwich City (7.30pm).

*all kick-off at 8pm, unless stated otherwise.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Recent findings suggest that jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Recent findings suggest that bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

Aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight new signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

The visitors have arrived in south London.

We've made it to South East London 👋 pic.twitter.com/nh8Fpa37xT.

We’re bringing you the action from the pick of tonight’s EFL Cup games but there are also four games kicking off at 7.45pm:.

Crystal Palace vs Middlesbrough.

Keeper Filip Marschall is making his debut while Jensen Metcalfe is back in the squad after his red card against Bolton was overturned on appeal.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the upcoming season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!
