Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4621 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

According to recent reports, hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso noted: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

It has been revealed that “But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

Recent findings suggest that “It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

According to recent reports, “Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the concern yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Industry observers note that hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is at the moment on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

According to recent reports, it is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a upcoming reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

In a recent development, “Before the season, I stated to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

Sources indicate that “Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

Industry observers note that while his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he remarked. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

Recent findings suggest that it was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

According to recent reports, I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

According to recent reports, we can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

According to recent reports, eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

According to recent reports, and as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”.

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

According to recent reports, you might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

In a recent development, that had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Industry observers note that bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well.

Sources indicate that within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

According to recent reports, tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Recent findings suggest that pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Sources indicate that andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

According to recent reports, so at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

In a recent development, apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

According to recent reports, that’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

In a recent development, this is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

It has been revealed that there is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472.

In a recent development, A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Sources indicate that morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez introduced the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

Recent findings suggest that we’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

In a recent development, xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

Industry observers note that we are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

Matt Crooks is absolutely massive.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a substantial buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

It has been revealed that dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Sources indicate that I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a newly introduced chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

According to recent reports, there have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Borussia Mönchengladbach head coach Alexander Blessin has highlighted his initiative to get a result against unbeaten Borussia Dortmund.

The two Borussias clash in the Bundesliga on Saturday afternoon, with bottom club Gladbach in desperate need of a victory with just one from their opening nine.

Sources indicate that “Dortmund obviously have enormous individual quality,” explained Blessin. “They have strong spells time and again, but there are also moments when you can get the better of them and perhaps right after the international break, that’s exactly when we can give them a hard time.”.

Relishing Saturday’s game, Blessin added: “We have to be highly focused and ready to give it our all for 90 minutes. It will be important to get away with it during the phases where Dortmund might have scoring opportunities or the upper hand. So that we can simply keep the game open until the 90th minute and then maybe score ourselves. It’s about having a high tolerance for suffering and showing the willingness to be really nasty.”.

Because Borussia-Park’s standing section has been increased, 54,909 fans will be in attendance on Saturday, beating the 54,042 record. “It’s going to be great,” added Blessin. “We’re looking forward to the game against a really good opponent, again whom we’ll give our all.”.

El Chadaille Bitshiabu (21) has played just 21 minutes for Galatasaray in 2026/27 following his summer loan move from RB Leipzig, and now the Turkish side could be ready to end the Frenchman’s loan deal.

BILD cite Turkish reports that Galatasaray are ready to send Bitshiabu back to Leipzig after arriving at the Süper Lig leaders in poor condition, reportedly 110kg and a body fat percentage of 18 percent – thus, he’s barely featured for Okan Buruk.

It’s vital to note that Bitshiabu also takes up one of the foreign spots in Galatasaray’s squad, although BILD add that there have been no discussions between the two clubs regarding an early termination.

According to recent reports, bitshiabu played 1,127 minutes across 21 Bundesliga games in 2024/25, but played just half that across 11 league games in 2025/26 under Ole Werner. Should the central defender return, then it’s likely that he will be shipped out on loan once again, with French outfit RC Lens one club that came close to signing the defender last summer, but that moved collapsed after both clubs failed to agree on the final conditions of the loan.

According to recent reports, speaking exclusively to t-mobile, Bayern president Herbert Hainer discussed Kompany’s approach. “Vincent Kompany truly brings a clear vision and a strong personality and, ultimately, it’s crucial what energy he unleashes in our team game after game. Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane became the first Bundesliga player to win the Ballon d’Or in 30 years, lifting the prestigious trophy ahead of Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal. Speaking exclusively to t-online, Bayern president Herbert Hainer discussed the significance of Kane claiming the coveted prize, awarded to the world’s best footballer, for both him and Germany’s record champions.

According to recent reports, “The significance of this cannot be overstated, both for Harry Kane and for Bayern and the entire Bundesliga,” explained Hainer. “We have the World Player of the Year in Germany, that’s an international exclamation mark. On Bayern’s club media channels, we shattered all previous records in terms of reach that day.

In a recent development, “Harry has developed even further here. For him, it wasn’t just an award for one season, but for his achievements over the past few years – as a footballer and as a person. He’s a role model off the pitch as well. Furthermore, he’s shown that at Bayern, you can achieve anything individually.”.

Kane returned 73 games across all competitions for both Bayern and England last season, and he’s already in unstoppable form this term, plundering 10 goals and providing a further 10 assists in 15 appearances across all competitions for die Rekordmeister.

📖 Baca

Tech Report: Former Old Firm rivals reveal how clubs walked a fine line between rivalry and respect...and even stopped by for tea and sympathy in times of trouble!

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1359 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Industry observers note that they have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm.
  • Sources indicate that they have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026.

Industry observers note that they have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm. Yet in the autumn of 2026 they cavort around Toryglen with an almost juvenile vigour.

Sources indicate that they have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm. Yet they are outlining plans and strategy for a vital, growing movement.

The two meetings are separated by two sets of stairs. On the ground level, men of pensionable age and beyond play walking football. Just above sit Campbell Ogilvie, former secretary of Rangers and president of the Scottish FA, and Eric Riley, once organization secretary and director of Celtic.

They are both on the board of Walking Football Scotland, an organisation that now has more than 5,000 people playing the game across 160 clubs, with participants ranging from 40 to 93.

The venerable statesmen of the Scottish game may be perceived to be rivals, but only in matters on the pitch. They sit in an office in the south side of Glasgow and reminisce about how they first met 50 years ago when playing five-a-sides and then renewed that rivalry in their professional life.

As the Glasgow rivals now seem regularly at odds, both men recalled a time when friendship was paramount amid the sporting mayhem.

Former Rangers secretary Campbell Ogilvie and ex-Celtic director Eric Riley are firm friends.

‘The two clubs always had a good relationship back in those days,’ said Ogilvie, now 76 and still playing football. ‘We wanted to beat each other — naturally. But off the field we had a very close relationship.’.

He told a remarkable story that backs that assertion.

Recent findings suggest that ‘There was one day I was at Ibrox in the early 1980s when the team was not doing so well. The phone rang and it was Sean Fallon, Jock Stein’s former Celtic assistant. I had known Sean from my days with the Scottish League and he said: “I know you’re going through a rocky spell, so I’m coming over for a cup of tea”.

‘Over he comes. So there was a very close relationship in those days. I’m not there now and for all I know there still is. But certainly, when I was there and Eric was at Celtic, we could talk to each other.’.

It has been revealed that riley, 69, agreed: ‘Absolutely. John McClelland (former Rangers chairman) was one we could talk to. And Martin (Bain, former chief executive) I suppose, when he came along a bit later. Between myself and Peter Lawwell (former Celtic chief executive and chairman) the relationship between the clubs off the field was actually quite strong. But on the field we still wanted to win.’.

Ogilvie added: ‘There was a respect. And I go back to the Willie Waddells and the Willie Thorntons, there was that respect. More recently that was there with the likes of Jack McGinn and so on.

‘We had a good relationship but it’s fair to say that there was no social media in those days. You know all the toxic stuff that can bring.’.

The traits of respect and sporting competitiveness have been obvious in both men since they first met half a century ago. ‘We played five-a-side football at Scotstoun before the football careers started. It was just casual games,’ said Ogilvie. ‘We were in our early 20s. Eric was an accountant and I think those games were arranged through accountants.

‘I played youth football when I was 16 and, 60 years down the line, playing football is still a major part of my life.’.

According to recent reports, ogilvie began walking football eight years ago and Riley soon after. ‘I suffer from Parkinson’s, amongst other things,’ noted Riley. ‘I was getting assistance through Stobhill Hospital and the physiotherapist there, who specialises in Parkinson’s patients, got in touch to say there was a project going on at Toryglen where they were playing walking football and assessing you to see what the benefits may or may not be.’.

Ogilvie and Riley are both on the board of Walking Football and have played a substantial role in its rise.

It has been revealed that riley agreed to take part. ‘I really enjoyed it because you are back playing football again, you have the camaraderie and you have the home baking which I never really get at home.’.

According to recent reports, riley had a hip replacement in March and admitted: ‘I have not played since then. I miss it. I play a few other things which are more and more difficult. I play tennis.’.

It has been revealed that his tennis history is illustrious as he played with Judy Murray in Scottish championships. ‘She went off to the tour and I went off to university,’ says Riley. He is unstinting in his praise of the woman who became the mother of the No1 in men’s singles and men’s doubles.

The repartee between Riley and Ogilvie is relaxed but both men have a resolve to grow walking football. Their task has been helped by bookmakers William Hill stepping in with sponsorship.

The benefits of the sport stretch beyond the physical. Ogilvie gave his own experience.

‘When you have finished working, there is a void, not mixing with people, not being with people, and walking football certainly has helped me fill that. Hopefully it helps me keep a bit fitter too,’ he said.

Ogilvie pointed out: ‘The issues you tend to encounter are health. Grief is another one. There are quite a few of the guys who have lost their wives and quite a few who are just sitting on the sofa watching Homes Under the Hammer.’.

Walking football, too, has attracted a large cadre of women. ‘One of the things that stood out for me was the number of females playing,’ stated Riley. ‘I went along to my first session and there were four female players, three of whom had never kicked a football in their life previously. Walking football got them involved and they really enjoyed it.’.

Walking football has made giant leaps in Scotland but the next step is to collate data so cases for funding will be made unanswerable.

It has been revealed that ‘We need facts or what is called data,’ noted Ogilvie. ‘We are trying to do some studies with universities to get that data — physical and mental — and get it to the government. We want to prove the benefits and then we could make this prescriptive through surgeries.

‘We see the benefits day to day anecdotally but that doesn’t bring you the data. Sponsorship helps.

Walking Football attracts thousands of participants at clubs across the country.

It has been revealed that ‘The university studies won’t come overnight because they need to be detailed. But if we could get to the stage where we could prove the benefits, then the NHS and the government would see that proof in black and white.’.

Industry observers note that this is all serious and proper. But both men were keen to emphasise that the game was fun. Ogilvie said: ‘When I started, I asked someone: “How would you sum up walking football?” He said to me: “It’s a cross between watching Barcelona and the Gurkha warriors”.’.

He added: ‘I loved when at the end of an over-75s tournament one player stated to another: “Good game, son”.’.

The football world has thus moved into a new era. But some things cannot change. Ogilvie noted: ‘One of my grandsons, who is 10, came along to watch a session and said two things. Firstly, it is a bit more intense than he thought and second there are no pink boots.’.

Riley chimed in: ‘That would be an affront, that would be unacceptable.’.

Even in walking football some things are a step too far.

In a recent development, ■ Eric Riley and Campbell Ogilvie were speaking at the announcement of William Hill as official sponsor of Walking Football Scotland. To find your nearest game visit walkingfootballscotland.org.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bayern Munich legend and honorary president Uli Hoeneß believes Jürgen Klopp can restore the discipline and hunger he feels have been missing from the German national team.
  • In a recent development, “I think he will bring discipline and hunger back in,” Hoeneß said.
  • Klopp’s Germany delivered their clearest statement yet on Monday night, thrashing the Netherlands 5-0 at Berlin’s Olympiastadion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich legend and honorary president Uli Hoeneß believes Jürgen Klopp can restore the discipline and hunger he feels have been missing from the German national team. Speaking at the Sport BILD Awards, Hoeneß backed the Germany head coach to impose his personality on the team while stressing that the rebuilding process will require patience.

In a recent development, “I think he will bring discipline and hunger back in,” Hoeneß said. “He is hungry himself. But I didn’t expect him to lay hands on everything to move quickly. We need to give him time. I also expect that many things will improve under Per Mertesacker, who is now overseeing the youth setup.”.

Klopp’s Germany delivered their clearest statement yet on Monday night, thrashing the Netherlands 5-0 at Berlin’s Olympiastadion. The emphatic victory secured top spot in Nations League Group A2 and a place in the quarter-finals, giving Germany a significant result as Klopp continues to reshape the national team.

Hoeneß’s comments on hunger were not restricted to Klopp or the German national team. The 74-year-old argued that German football has been affected by broader social changes, recalling the environment in which he developed as a young player.

“I used to play football on the street after school, from two in the afternoon until nightfall,” Hoeneß noted. “That no longer exists today. We live in a country where most people are doing very well. I see this as the greatest danger for our football as well. If someone comes from Brazil, Portugal, or Argentina, they want to climb the social ladder. That is what we lack.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We must learn again to work hard if we want to be successful,” Hoeneß continued. “That applies not only to footballers, but to the whole country.”.

Industry observers note that for Hoeneß, Klopp’s task therefore extends beyond tactical adjustments or short-term results. The Bayern honorary president believes restoring the mentality he associates with successful German teams will be just as important as the structural work being undertaken in Germany’s youth setup.

FEATURE | Six winners from the Germany U21 November 2026 international break

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3850 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, antonio Di Salvo’s Germany U21s managed to conclude their 2026 calendar year with two consecutive friendly defeats during the November international break, falling 2-1 to Belgium in Essen before surrendering a second-half lead in a bizarre 3-2 loss to Croatia in Rijeka.
  • While such results certainly weren’t what Di Salvo and his staff had envisioned, the fact that neither result carried competitive consequences should temper the disappointment.
  • It has been revealed that the Belgium encounter featured some encouraging attacking football, particularly from players who had only recently entered or returned to the U21 setup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, antonio Di Salvo’s Germany U21s managed to conclude their 2026 calendar year with two consecutive friendly defeats during the November international break, falling 2-1 to Belgium in Essen before surrendering a second-half lead in a bizarre 3-2 loss to Croatia in Rijeka. The results brought an abrupt end to an impressive eight-match winning streak and left the DFB youngsters with plenty to contemplate ahead of next summer’s UEFA European U21 Championship.

While such results certainly weren’t what Di Salvo and his staff had envisioned, the fact that neither result carried competitive consequences should temper the disappointment. Moreover, the international break wasn’t nearly as disappointing as the scorelines suggested. Our Get German Football News analysis of two matches yields just one fewer ‘winner’ than our long-form check on Jürgen Klopp’s senior men’s team.

It has been revealed that the Belgium encounter featured some encouraging attacking football, particularly from players who had only recently entered or returned to the U21 setup. The Germans repeatedly created dangerous situations through aggressive pressing, midfield combinations, and individual attacking initiative. Unfortunately, defensive lapses and insufficient precision in front of goal undermined much of the positive work.

Sources indicate that tuesday’s fixture against Croatia proved an entirely different proposition. Torrential rainfall, thick fog, and a playing surface that gradually transformed into something resembling a collection of small lakes made meaningful football almost impossible. Di Salvo’s team nevertheless recovered from a 1-0 halftime deficit to take the lead before the hosts scored twice in the final 25 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that the conditions prompted the German U21 coach to question whether anything meaningful could be learned from the encounter. Speaking at the post-match press conference attended by Get German Football News, Di Salvo expressed relief that the players had escaped injury and emphasized that the earlier Belgium match offered a more useful opportunity for analysis.

There is another key consideration.

In a recent development, the November squad had been weakened considerably by injuries and withdrawals. Established U21 contributors such as Tom Bischof, Lennart Karl, and Remarked El Mala were also unavailable because of their involvement with Jürgen Klopp’s senior national team. The absence of captain Nicolo Tresoldi, who suffered a concussion in training, required Di Salvo to make significant alterations to his attacking plans.

The personnel difficulties opened opportunities for several players attempting to establish themselves at Germany’s highest youth level.

Some seized their chances rather emphatically.

It has been revealed that the author is thus pleased to present six winners from the November international break. The selections take account of individual performances, tactical contributions, and the extent to which players improved their standing ahead of next summer’s European Championship.

Recent findings suggest that few players entered November with more to gain than Cajetan Lenz. The 20-year-old made his Germany U21 debut against Belgium after previously earning nine appearances at U20 level and below. His promotion came at a particularly interesting stage in his club career.

It has been revealed that lenz emerged as one of the most impressive young midfielders in the 2. Bundesliga during his breakthrough campaign at Bochum, making 31 league appearances and attracting considerable interest from top-flight clubs. Get German Football News identified the youngster as a potential Bayer Leverkusen transfer target in its December 2025 transfer primer. Eintracht Frankfurt also pursued the midfielder before Hoffenheim ultimately secured his services.

The move has nevertheless presented some unforeseen difficulties.

Sources indicate that as GGFN examined following Lenz’s U21 debut, the midfielder has struggled to break into Christian Ilzer’s Bundesliga team, accumulating just three minutes of league football this season. His performances for Germany therefore carried particular significance. Lenz operated alongside Noël Aseko in central midfield against Belgium, contributing to several encouraging attacking sequences and repeatedly driving forward to support the team’s more advanced players.

Industry observers note that his energetic movement was especially notable during Germany’s stronger first-half periods, when the hosts attempted to establish control through combinations involving Damar, Brunner, and the left-sided players. The debutant’s willingness to carry possession forward and participate in attacking movements offered an encouraging contrast to his limited opportunities at club level.

Industry observers note that di Salvo was clearly impressed. Speaking at the post-match press conference in Essen, the coach specifically identified Lenz as one of the players who had made a positive impression upon the coaching staff.

In a recent development, “It’s a little early to discuss the [2027 UEFA U21] European championship roster,” Di Salvo remarked on Friday. “There are still many games to be played and many lads who, of course, aren’t here. And yet, there are some who – with their performances – have managed to make a mark with their impressions.”.

Sources indicate that “Namely, Cajetan Lenz, who played a very good game today,” Di Salvo continued. “He’s had very little playing time and I was thus pleased to see him log 85 minutes today. It was good that he could plow on through. From time to time he lacked clarity and the last pass was somewhat imprecise.

In a recent development, “But in general, he delivered a fantastic performance,” Di Salvo concluded. “He really ran a lot and marched forward. With that, particularly in light of his lack of playing time, we’re really satisfied with him.”.

Lenz followed his impressive debut with another encouraging appearance against Croatia. The Hoffenheim professional remained active despite the deteriorating conditions, nearly breaking into the penalty area early in the second half and heading narrowly wide from a Tom Rothe cross in the 51st minute.

According to recent reports, two minutes later, he provided the decisive touch from Damar’s free kick that enabled Moerstedt to score Germany’s equalizer. The youngster continued his attacking involvement throughout the second half, although he would undoubtedly have preferred a better outcome when Pejcinovic’s 82nd-minute shot rebounded into his path.

His failure to convert that opportunity represented one of Germany’s more frustrating moments during the final stages, but two consecutive 7/10 ratings constitute an impressive return for a player making his first two appearances at this level.

According to recent reports, lenz himself appeared determined to maintain realistic expectations when speaking to GGFN in the mixed zone after the Belgium encounter. The midfielder emphasized his gratitude for the opportunity while acknowledging that he remained a challenger for a regular position.

Di Salvo’s subsequent praise suggests that the youngster has already made considerable progress toward that objective.

Recent findings suggest that brunner’s inclusion hardly requires justification given his consistency across both matches. The former Germany U17 World Champion earned 8/10 ratings from GGFN against both Belgium and Croatia, emerging as one of the few German attackers capable of producing threatening moments throughout the international break.

Recent findings suggest that brunner’s November responsibilities were considerably different from those he had assumed earlier in the qualification campaign. As GGFN examined in its October Germany U21 Tactics Check, Di Salvo had previously enjoyed considerable success with a versatile attacking trio consisting of Brunner, Tresoldi, and Dzenan Pejcinovic. Tresoldi’s absence forced the coach to reconsider how best to organize his forwards.

Against Belgium, Brunner took on the central attacking assignment while Muhammed Damar moved onto the left. The Monaco professional began energetically and continued to involve himself in Germany’s attacking combinations, even if the hosts frequently lacked precision with their final deliveries.

One of Brunner’s more important contributions came in the 24th minute, when he drew the foul that provided Damar with the opportunity to equalize from a free kick. Brunner subsequently participated in the attacking sequence that resulted in Damar’s second effort against the crossbar in the 58th minute.

It has been revealed that the youngster continued searching for a goal after Damar’s substitution, attempting an acrobatic finish in the 71st minute and producing several further incursions into the Belgian penalty area. The Croatia match offered an opportunity to demonstrate an additional dimension of his game.

Brunner began alongside Pejcinovic in what appeared to be a narrow 4-2-2-2. At halftime, however, Di Salvo introduced Max Moerstedt and deliberately shifted Brunner onto the left. The adjustment worked exceptionally well. Brunner became one of Germany’s most productive attacking players after the interval. His delivery for Pejcinovic’s 60th-minute goal supplied the visitors with a 2-1 lead, and the Monaco professional also struck the post during Germany’s strongest attacking spell.

Di Salvo deliberately and justifiably singled the 20-year-old out for praise after the break had officially concluded.

While Brunner stands out for his consistency, Damar can reasonably claim to have delivered the outstanding individual performance of the international break. The Wolfsburg attacker returned to the U21 starting XI against Belgium following an extended absence and promptly produced a display worthy of GGFN’s Player of the Match award and a 9/10 rating.

It proved quite the joy to observe Damar’s stated determination to make the most of his national-team comeback manifest itself on the pitch. The 22-year-old began the first fixture shot out of a cannon and proceeded to cover nearly every blade of grass on the pitch. Beginning on the left wing, he frequently rotated into central areas and occasionally appeared on the opposite flank, creating considerable difficulty for the Belgian defenders attempting to track him.

His equalizer in the 25th minute was particularly memorable.

Industry observers note that having earned another opportunity from a dead ball, Damar cleverly drove his free kick underneath the jumping Belgian defensive wall. The technique was unusual, the execution excellent, and the subsequent celebration both touching and unforgettable.

Industry observers note that he wasn’t finished. A second free kick in the 38th minute was tipped onto the crossbar. He struck the woodwork again in the 58th following an excellent attacking combination with Pejcinovic and Brunner. There were stretches of the match during which Damar appeared determined to generate virtually every meaningful German attacking opportunity himself.

Speaking to GGFN and other journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Damar explained the instinctive decision behind his free-kick goal, expressed frustration about his missed opportunities, and spoke enthusiastically about the pride he takes in representing Germany.

Industry observers note that his performance against Croatia was considerably less influential but that had much to do with the fact that the waterlogged surface made life particularly difficult for a technical attacker who relies upon close control, quick changes of direction, and precise passing. Damar nevertheless remained involved in Germany’s attacking moves and supplied the free kick from which Cajetan Lenz helped create Moerstedt’s equalizer.

The author still saw fit to award him a 6/10 in Rijeka.

Overall, Damar’s international comeback constituted an unequivocal success.

What a difference 45 minutes can make. Moerstedt’s November international break began with an unexpected call-up following Nicolo Tresoldi’s injury withdrawal and concluded with his first Germany U21 goal and a GGFN Player of the Match award.

Sources indicate that the Hoffenheim striker only joined the squad after the international break had begun, making his U21 debut as an 86th-minute substitute against Belgium. There was little time for him to influence that fixture. GGFN awarded Moerstedt a 5/10, reflecting his brief involvement rather than any particularly poor performance.

In a recent development, croatia presented a substantially greater opportunity. With Germany trailing 1-0 at halftime, Di Salvo introduced the youngster as part of a four-player substitution package. The coach wanted more presence inside the Croatian penalty area and consequently repositioned Brunner onto the left.

Moerstedt responded almost immediately. Germany emerged with greater attacking purpose, and the Hoffenheim striker began involving himself in combinations with the midfielders and his fellow forwards.

In the 53rd minute, Lenz redirected Damar’s free kick toward Moerstedt inside the Croatian penalty area. The striker’s initial effort was blocked, but he reacted rapidly enough to recover possession and convert at the second attempt.

In a recent development, the equalizer changed the direction of the match and helped establish the momentum that eventually produced Germany’s second goal. There was much to admire about Moerstedt’s performance beyond the finish itself.

The 20-year-old offered the type of physical presence and determination inside the box that Germany had lacked during the opening half. He remained available for deliveries despite the increasingly treacherous surface and helped occupy Croatian defenders as Brunner and Pejcinovic enjoyed greater freedom in attack.

It has been revealed that moerstedt’s first goal came in only his second U21 appearance, and his performance in Rijeka earned him an 8/10 rating. With Tresoldi expected to remain an notable figure in Di Salvo’s looks, the competition for the central attacking position will undoubtedly be intense.

Moerstedt has nevertheless made an impressive opening argument for further opportunities.

It has been revealed that the next place goes to a midfielder who quietly delivered two of Germany’s more consistent performances during an otherwise difficult international break. Noël Aseko earned 7/10 ratings against both Belgium and Croatia, providing vital energy and physical commitment in central midfield.

In a recent development, aseko’s contribution deserves particular recognition because of the changes surrounding him. Di Salvo’s squad was missing several key midfield options, while the promotion of Tom Bischof to the senior national team and other withdrawals required the coach to assemble a revised central partnership.

Aseko consequently began both November fixtures alongside U21 debutant Cajetan Lenz. The pair faced an interesting challenge against Belgium. Germany wanted to press aggressively, regain possession high up the pitch, and support the attacking players through quick combinations. This frequently required the midfielders to advance into dangerous areas, leaving the defensive unit with considerable responsibility when the Belgians escaped pressure.

Aseko demonstrated his ability to carry possession forward as early as the sixth minute, accelerating past several Belgian opponents before combining with Brunner. His physical approach also produced an early yellow card, but the midfielder continued participating energetically in Germany’s attacking and defensive work. The partnership with Lenz was particularly encouraging.

Industry observers note that aseko contributed greater physicality and direct running, while his Hoffenheim colleague frequently assumed responsibility for progressing possession and connecting with the attacking players. In the Croatia match, with the playing surface progressively deteriorating, Aseko and Lenz were frequently required to abandon conventional passing combinations in favor of more direct and physically demanding actions.

Aseko nevertheless remained involved in Germany’s second-half revival. Immediately after the restart, the midfielder found himself in a shooting position following a corner, although his effort was blocked before reaching goal. His work helped Germany establish the territorial advantage that eventually produced Moerstedt’s equalizer and Pejcinovic’s second goal.

Industry observers note that aseko departed in the 64th minute, having again supplied an energetic performance despite the increasingly difficult conditions. Aseko continues to demonstrate why he deserves consideration for a regular place in that system. There are flashier candidates for an international-break winners list, but two strong performances alongside a newly introduced midfield partner merit recognition.

Sources indicate that the sixth and final inclusion requires a little explanation. Pejcinovic received a disappointing 4/10 rating from GGFN against Belgium, having struggled to impose himself consistently on the match. He nevertheless followed that performance with a considerably more encouraging display in Croatia, earning an 8/10 after scoring Germany’s second goal and producing several other noteworthy attacking contributions.

The contrast is interesting, particularly when considered alongside Di Salvo’s assessment of the Belgium encounter. Pejcinovic had already enjoyed an excellent qualification campaign before November. As GGFN documented following Germany’s decisive victory over Georgia, the Stuttgart professional scored twice to help secure direct qualification for next summer’s European Championship.

In a recent development, his transfer from Wolfsburg to Stuttgart earlier in the season also represented an notable step in his professional development. As the striker acknowledged in an October interview , however, establishing himself at Bundesliga level for his new club has presented challenges.

The November friendlies provided another opportunity to demonstrate his qualities. Against Belgium, Pejcinovic sometimes struggled with his timing and final deliveries. An attempted pass to Anton Kade early in the second half was particularly inaccurate, while his involvement in Germany’s attacking moves did not always translate into threatening opportunities.

There were nevertheless positive contributions. Pejcinovic helped initiate the 58th-minute sequence in which Brunner released Damar for another attempt against the crossbar. His movement and willingness to participate in combinations also provided Germany with an additional presence between midfield and attack.

Di Salvo was keen to emphasize these aspects when asked about the striker’s performance at the post-match press conference.

In a recent development, “No, that thought didn’t occur to me at all,” Di Salvo answered when questioned by the Rheinische Post about Dzenan Pejcinovic’s comparatively tepid performance on Friday night. “He trained strongly and scored his goals.”.

“We found him to be confident in the goal-shooting drills,” Di Salvo continued. “And we found the distance covered stats from not just Dzenan but the entire team today to be exceptionally good.”.

“He was always running and strong on the press,” Di Salvo concluded. “That’s what I judge to be most important. That was good. He participated in the build up play in the first half and was able to help out the play on the wings. We found that well-executed by the entire team.”.

It has been revealed that the coach’s comments provide a useful reminder that the assessment of an attacking player cannot rest exclusively upon his finishing or goalscoring contributions. Against Croatia, Pejcinovic offered considerably more of both.

In a recent development, an excellent opportunity went begging in the 18th minute after Damar released him into space, but the Stuttgart forward continued working energetically despite the difficult playing conditions. His perseverance was rewarded after Germany’s halftime adjustments.

With Brunner operating from the left and Moerstedt providing an additional penalty-area presence, Pejcinovic found himself benefiting from a more productive attacking structure. The Stuttgart professional finished Brunner’s cross in the 60th minute to give Germany a 2-1 lead.

Further contributions followed at both ends of the pitch. Pejcinovic helped defend two Croatian corners at the near post and continued seeking opportunities to threaten the opposition goal. His excellent shot from distance in the 82nd minute forced Toni Silic into a save, with the rebound presenting Lenz with an opportunity to equalize before Croatia’s eventual winning goal.

The 8/10 GGFN rating reflected a much more complete attacking performance.

Pejcinovic remains an vital member of Germany’s U21 squad, and November demonstrated both the value of his established attacking qualities and the considerable benefits of playing alongside forwards capable of complementing his movement.

According to recent reports, germany’s November international break offered plenty of interesting tactical material, even if the extraordinary conditions in Croatia necessarily limit how much one should attempt to extract from the second fixture. Di Salvo’s personnel difficulties were particularly significant.

Sources indicate that the absence of Tresoldi removed an established attacking reference point, while injuries and senior national-team promotions required substantial changes to the midfield and forward positions. The result was a Germany side that retained some familiar attacking principles but frequently looked different from the one that had secured European Championship qualification in October.

Germany began the Belgium encounter in a nominal 4-2-3-1, with Brunner leading the line, Damar operating from the left, Kade on the right, and Pejcinovic occupying the central attacking position behind the striker. Lenz and Aseko formed the central midfield pairing.

The basic structure proved rather fluid. Damar frequently moved away from his starting position, seeking possession in central areas and occasionally appearing on the right. Brunner and Pejcinovic also pushed together into advanced positions, temporarily giving the formation the appearance of a more conventional 4-4-2. The central midfielders were encouraged to advance and participate in Germany’s attempts to recover possession high up the pitch.

These movements helped produce several encouraging attacking sequences. The problem, unfortunately, concerned the spaces Germany left behind whenever Belgium managed to escape the initial press. Julien Duranville’s eighth-minute opener demonstrated the danger. Lucas Stassin beat Collins on the right and supplied the delivery that allowed Duranville to finish from close range.

The hosts subsequently established greater territorial control, but their commitment to attacking occasionally invited further Belgian opportunities. Collins’ misplaced pass in the 44th minute nearly produced another goal, with Stassin ultimately striking the post.

Di Salvo’s team appeared somewhat more cautious after the restart, although Damar’s movement and individual initiative continued to generate threatening situations. The final result nevertheless reflected Germany’s difficulties in balancing attacking ambition with defensive protection.

Belgium’s second goal arrived immediately after both coaches made several substitutions, with the German defensive structure unable to respond quickly enough to a newly introduced attacker. Di Salvo subsequently praised his team’s pressing at the post-match press conference but acknowledged that the defending and missed opportunities had not been good enough.

Industry observers note that the Croatia encounter was considerably more difficult to assess. Di Salvo made just one starting change, replacing Collins with Linus Gechter in central defence. Poor visibility made the precise opening formation difficult to determine, although Germany appeared to operate in a narrow 4-2-2-2.

According to recent reports, the narrow attacking shape may have been influenced by the extraordinary circumstances. Thick fog made it difficult for players to locate teammates, while standing water increasingly disrupted attempts to circulate possession through the wider areas. The Germans initially attempted to play through the conditions, with mixed results.

It has been revealed that damar’s excellent pass to Pejcinovic in the 18th minute created a clear opportunity, but Croatia subsequently took the lead through Adrian Segecic. The most important tactical development occurred at halftime. Di Salvo introduced Moerstedt, Collins, Morgalla, and Rothe. The changes allowed Brunner to move onto the left while Moerstedt assumed a more pronounced central attacking role.

Lineup—Germany U21 vs. Croatia (46th minute).

The adjustment immediately improved Germany’s attacking options. Moerstedt supplied the penalty-area presence necessary to capitalize upon deliveries and loose balls, while Brunner became considerably more influential when attacking from the left.

Lenz’s involvement in the equalizer illustrated the continued importance of Germany’s midfielders in supporting attacks, while Brunner’s cross for Pejcinovic’s goal demonstrated the increased productivity of the revised attacking arrangement.

The hosts’ subsequent equalizer, scored after the ball became stranded in a large puddle, served as another reminder that conventional tactical analysis has its limitations when the conditions become this extreme.

Sources indicate that the most encouraging developments concern Germany’s attacking options. Brunner demonstrated his versatility, Damar reaffirmed his attacking quality, and Moerstedt made an excellent initial case for a more substantial role in the U21 squad.

Pejcinovic remains a productive striker who can contribute beyond goalscoring, while Lenz and Aseko supplied an encouraging central midfield partnership despite the absence of several established alternatives.

Recent findings suggest that the November defeats should not be dismissed, particularly given the defensive shortcomings that were evident against Belgium. Yet neither should the individual developments be overlooked.

Germany have already qualified for next summer’s European Championship, and Di Salvo now has several more footballers who have demonstrated that they deserve consideration when the competition for tournament places intensifies.

Two defeats, six winners, and more than a few selection headaches.

Not necessarily the conclusion to the international year one might have hoped for.

But certainly not a complete waste of time, either.

Dino Toppmöller, who left his role at French Ligue 1 side RC Lens in September, has been linked with a possible move back to the Bundesliga according to Sport BILD.

Cologne who only gathered nine points from the first nine games of the Bundesliga are contemplating a managerial change and the former Eintracht Frankfurt coach is on top of the list.

Toppmöller was dismissed from his role at Lens not because of results on the pitch but because of his loyalty to his assistant coach, whom he felt was wrongly terminated.

The Billy Goats will face Bayern Munich on Friday, but the next game against Elversberg on November 28 is expected to determine the future of 38-year-old coach Wagner.

Industry observers note that toppmöller was under consideration in Cologne last summer, but an agreement wasn’t reached on his salary. According to Sport Bild, the 45-year-old would be open to renewed talks. In addition to Toppmöller, Christian Eichner (most recently at Karlsruhe), Horst Steffen (most recently at Werder Bremen) and David Hubert (Union Saint-Gilloise) are possible candidates for the role if Wagner departs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

It has been revealed that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

In a recent development, A team reimagined, a manager freshly rolled out and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

Recent findings suggest that for Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he mentioned. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Industry observers note that indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

At the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi said later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

“There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

According to recent reports, spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Industry observers note that hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Industry observers note that some surprised faces then when Moyes said later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”.

The game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes noted that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

Recent findings suggest that in the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

Industry observers note that the first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

Industry observers note that de Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He mentioned that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

According to recent reports, speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender noted: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and showed that mentality again in the second half.

“We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”.

It has been revealed that tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

According to recent reports, boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

“We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” says Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

Sources indicate that “I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

According to recent reports, alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

💡 Key Takeaways
