  • Since the beginning of the month in Spain, referees have started making themselves available for interview after matches to explain decisions and improve transparency.
  • It has led to people here asking why Scotland’s whistlers aren’t doing the same — and those questions are perfectly valid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:39 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:46 EST, 13 November 2026.

Since the beginning of the month in Spain, referees have started making themselves available for interview after matches to explain decisions and improve transparency.

It has led to people here asking why Scotland’s whistlers aren’t doing the same — and those questions are perfectly valid.

Back in August 2023, leading official John Beaton addressed calls for greater openness around VAR and gave the impression the refereeing firmament were in favour of a fresh spirit of glasnost.

‘Anything to explain how we are arriving at decisions and anything we can do to show people what we do on a Saturday and what happens in the VAR centre, we absolutely welcome,’ he remarked.

‘The more transparency, the better. The more questions we get, the more answers we can provide and, we hope, get to a better place,’.

Recent findings suggest that that was followed by newly introduced head of refereeing Willie Collum’s VAR show on YouTube the following season. At that point, there seemed a real move to lift the lid and build confidence in our men in black. There was talk of Collum doing his programme more than once a month and suggestions referees might even be open to being interviewed post-match in the right circumstances.

Unfortunately, though, all that has come to nothing and last term — in which controversial decisions had a huge effect on the title race — feels like it could become an obstacle in the way of progress.

Head of Referees Willie Collum should be applauded for speaking up on the SFA VAR show.

It needn’t be, though. There has always been a feeling among referees that being put in front of the cameras carried danger. SFA Ian Maxwell has also spoken about the game being subject to ‘fairly hysterical commentary’ when something bad happens.

Recent findings suggest that the media environment here is nowhere near as febrile as in Spain, though. It has four newspapers dedicated to sport alone. There are countless chat reveals on council telly full of talking heads. Ages ago, news bulletins there had lipreaders telling viewers what coaches and players were saying on the park. Jose Mourinho is also back ruffling officials’ feathers at Real Madrid.

In a recent development, getting Spanish refs to a place where they feel ready to be interviewed has taken time. It has also taken extra cash for them from TV money and it can still go a lot further.

It has been revealed that A selected referee will speak to broadcast rights-holders only. And it’s not after every game. Only selected fixtures.

The SFA made real progress a couple of years back in lifting the curtain and should seek to rediscover that momentum — even though it won’t make the key issue of having to improve overall standards go away.

According to recent reports, since last year, the Spanish FA have been broadcasting their own YouTube show ‘Tiempo de Revision’ to address flashpoints. It should be said that it’s inferior to Collum’s broadcast in terms of content.

Sources indicate that it replays incidents against a musical backdrop with captions explaining the decisions. There is no in-game audio, no one like Collum putting himself out there.

Although some of his reasoning for massive calls was a bit suspect last term, that programme remains a platform to build from.

There is no reason why referees shouldn’t explain their decision-making after games here. Criticism they may or may not receive in the aftermath shouldn’t come into it.

If Spanish whistlers can go public, so can they.

Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, l’ex portiere dice: «Lo strapotere dell’Inter mi sembra evidente, per progetto e per forza degli interpreti. Milan e Juventus sono in una di quelle fasi che sembrano interlocutorie. Il Napoli è in difficoltà e mi dispiace. Ne verrà fuori, me lo auguro». Reina distingue così la forza dell’Inter dalla situazione delle altre formazioni citate.

Reina parla anche della classifica e dei due allenatori a cui è legato: «La Lazio è prima, il Como è quinto e su quelle panchine ci sono due miei amici che vedo e sento spesso. Gattuso mi ha segnato umanamente, però anche tatticamente ha proposte che mi hanno convinto.».

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost €800m was spent among Bundesliga clubs on signings in the summer, per Transfermarkt, but while Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund have splashed big on Ismael Saibari and Konstantinos Karetsas, there’s been some excellent signings throughout the 18 teams.

Get German Football News explores the five best….

Flourishing at RB Leipzig since returning to the club on loan in the summer, Christopher Nkunku has returned five goals and provided two assists since returning to the Saxony club. The Frenchman provided an assist against Borussia Mönchengladbach on his second debut before opening his account at the Red Bull Arena in Leipzig’s 5-0 victory over Hamburg. The 29-year-old then struck a hat-trick against Eintracht Frankfurt before adding a goal and assist to his 2026/27 tally against Augsburg prior to the international break. Often starting in a three-pronged attack alongside Romulo and Antonio Nusa/Tidiam Gomis, Nkunku is given the freedom to roam by Martin Demichelis, which makes his a nuisance for opposition defenders. Ranked in the 95th percentile for xGoals on target (4.14), Nkunku has proved clinical in front of goal, scoring five of his eight attempts on target.

Recent findings suggest that the Spaniard has big boots to fill following the departure of Alejandro Grimaldo, but the former Napoli man is settling into life at Bayer Leverkusen just fine. The 25-year-old has scored one goal and created a further four in his nine Bundesliga starts since swapping Italy for Germany. Equally adept at playing as the left-sided centre-back in a back three, or as the left-back or left-wing back in a back four/five, no defender ranks higher in the Bundesliga than Gutiérrez for assists and big chances created (eight) in Germany’s top flight this season.

Industry observers note that hennes Behrens at €3.5m is proving to be a steal for Augsburg, who are proving to be one of the Bundesliga’s best recruiters. Joining from Hoffenheim after spending last season on loan at Heidenheim, the 21-year-old is proving a useful weapon from left-back, where he’s registered three assists in nine Bundesliga outings this term. Possessing explosive pace and pinpoint crossing, Behrens is fast becoming one of the league’s most useful full-backs in the final third.

Industry observers note that re-joining Werder Bremen on loan after a failed spell abroad, Niclas Füllkrug is firing on all cylinders back at the Weserstadion. The 33-year-old sits at the top of the Bundesliga’s scoring charts this term having scored nine goals in as many appearances – seven of those have come from set-piece situations. Playing with a smile on his face once again, it’s great to see Füllkrug back to his best, which has also seen him return to the German national team. Carry on, and Bremen could well be competing for a place in Europe if the veteran goal-getter remains injury free and keeps up his output.

In a recent development, joining newly promoted Elversberg from Bayern Munich having spent last season on loan at 2. Bundesliga side Hertha Berlin, Maurice Krattenmacher has scored four goals and provided one assist in nine Bundesliga games this season – of which he’s only started four. The 21-year-old came off the bench to score a brace against Gladbach to secure a dramatic 4-3 victory for Vincent Wagner’s side, before netting against Bayern the following matchday with a superb curling effort. The attacking-midfielder also registered an assist and scored in wins of Augsburg and Mainz as the Bundesliga newcomers enjoy a magnificent start to their Bundesliga tenure.

Tresoldi o Endrick: chi servirebbe di più al Milan a gennaio?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (464 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Milannews

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manca sempre meno all'apertura del mercato invernale e in casa rossonera, dove si cerca un rinforzo importante in attacco, sono due i nomi più caldi che vengono fatti con maggiore insistenza, vale a dire quelli di Nicolò Tresoldi del Club Brugge e Endrick del Real Madrid.
  • Se a livello economico la loro valutazione è simile (intorno ai 60 milioni di euro), dal punto di vista tecnico e tattico sono molto distanti: Tresoldi è un vero centravanti con un grande fiuto del gol (ad oggi è già a quota 14 gol segnati in questa stagione).
  • Sources indicate that prendere Tresoldi vorrebbe dire dare a Ruben Amorim quel goleador che sta mancando finra al Milan, ma allo stesso tempo significherebbe mettere in discussione Gonçalo Ramos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manca sempre meno all'apertura del mercato invernale e in casa rossonera, dove si cerca un rinforzo importante in attacco, sono due i nomi più caldi che vengono fatti con maggiore insistenza, vale a dire quelli di Nicolò Tresoldi del Club Brugge e Endrick del Real Madrid. Si tratta di due giocatori completamente diversi e per questo sorge spontanea una domanda: chi tra i due servirebbe di più al Milan a gennaio?

Se a livello economico la loro valutazione è simile (intorno ai 60 milioni di euro), dal punto di vista tecnico e tattico sono molto distanti: Tresoldi è un vero centravanti con un grande fiuto del gol (ad oggi è già a quota 14 gol segnati in questa stagione). Il suo meglio lo dà negli ultimi 20 metri e in area di rigore dove sa muoversi alla grande grazie anche alla sua fisicità. Endrick è invece uno giocatore che agisce da trequarista o da seconda punta, è molto abile nell'uno contro uno e grazie alla sua enorme tecnica sa essere utile anche come uomo assist.

Sources indicate that prendere Tresoldi vorrebbe dire dare a Ruben Amorim quel goleador che sta mancando finra al Milan, ma allo stesso tempo significherebbe mettere in discussione Gonçalo Ramos. I due, in caso di necessità, potrebbero anche giocare insieme, però in linea di principio uno sarebbe l'alternativa dell'altro. Avrebbe senso spendere oltre 130 milioni di euro per due centravanti, di cui uno finirà quasi sempre in panchina? Con la partenza di Francesco Camarda in prestito che è ormai scritta, il portoghese avrà bisogno certamente di un altro giocatore con cui alternarsi, ma forse investire altri 60 milioni per prendere la sua alternativa potrebbe avere poco senso.

Sources indicate that nel Milan di Amorim, Endrick aumenterebbe notevolmente la qualità della trequarti milanista e potrebbe giocare senza problemi sia con Christian Pulisic che con Alphadjo Cisse. C'è però la questione che riguarda la formula del suo trasferimento: il Real Madrid, che per ora continua a ripetere di non volerlo dare via a gennaio (anche il Club Brugge sta facendo lo stesso per Tresoldi), non vorrebbe comunque perdere totalmente il controllo sul brasiliano e per questo vorrebbe inserire una clausola di recompra. Dunque il Diavolo dovrebbe spendere 60 milioni per prenderlo a titolo definitivo, ma in realtà il giocatore non sarebbe suo al 100%.

Chi servirebbe di più quindi al Milan? Molto dipende ovviamente da quello che cerca Amorim a cui spetterà l'ultima parola. Il tecnico portoghese ha più bisogno di un'alternativa di alto livello a Gonçalo Ramos oppure sarebbe più utile inserire un giocatore di qualità sulla trequarti che possa dare maggiore fantasia alla manovra milanista? Le prossime settimane saranno fondamentali per Amorim per capire chi potrebbe essere più utile al suo Diavolo tra Tresoldi ed Endrick.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that in his first press conference back from his illness-related absence, Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany offered an interesting perspective on Jamal Musiala’s impending return to competitive football.
  • Musiala is expected to return to Bayern’s matchday squad on Friday, provided he encounters no setbacks during Thursday’s final training session.
  • Recent findings suggest that the latest setback interrupted an encouraging return to competitive football.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in his first press conference back from his illness-related absence, Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany offered an interesting perspective on Jamal Musiala’s impending return to competitive football. The Belgian suggested that the German international could benefit from the changing expectations surrounding him. Speaking at Thursday’s pre-match press conference ahead of Bayern’s Bundesliga encounter with Köln, Kompany also addressed recent remarks from honorary president Uli Hoeneß concerning the 23-year-old’s long-term prospects.

Musiala is expected to return to Bayern’s matchday squad on Friday, provided he encounters no setbacks during Thursday’s final training session. The attacking midfielder has been sidelined since suffering a significant thigh injury while warming up for Germany’s UEFA Nations League encounter with the Netherlands in September.

Recent findings suggest that the latest setback interrupted an encouraging return to competitive football. Musiala has accumulated approximately 200 minutes this season, scoring in both of his starts. He opened the scoring in Bayern’s 5-0 Champions League victory over Bodø/Glimt and the 7-0 Bundesliga triumph over Union Berlin.

Recent findings suggest that musiala’s recovery has attracted additional attention following recent remarks from Uli Hoeneß questioning whether the midfielder can regain his previous performance level. Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen also raised questions about how the club might respond if Musiala’s performances were permanently affected. Sporting director Max Eberl sought to reassure supporters on Thursday, emphasizing the club’s continued belief in Musiala’s ability to rediscover his best form.

Kompany, meanwhile, adopted a different approach to the discussion. Rather than disagreeing with Bayern’s hierarchy, the Belgian emphasized that his responsibility as head coach requires him to maintain confidence in his players regardless of the concerns expressed elsewhere within the organization.

The Bayern trainer also suggested that Musiala’s changed circumstances could provide valuable motivation. Having previously enjoyed the status of an almost untouchable young star, the midfielder now has an opportunity to demonstrate his abilities without carrying precisely the same expectations.

Kompany drew a parallel between Musiala’s comeback and his own return following an extended absence due to illness. The coach expressed hope that both experiences could provide renewed energy for Bayern during the remainder of the season. The 40-year-old also praised Musiala’s determination throughout his rehabilitation, emphasizing that the youngster must ultimately demonstrate his recovery through performances on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that “We don’t have differing opinions,” Kompany added when questioned about Hoeneß’ comments on Musiala. “What we have is different roles. My role is to believe in all the players. That’s my role. It would be a catastrophe if I came here and stated that, for example, five specific players didn’t matter.”.

According to recent reports, “The fact that we have different roles is one of the things that function well at Bayern,” Kompany continued. “I have 100 percent respect for the opinions of the [club] hierarchy. I don’t have a problem with that. One has to put it into perspective and we can also utilize this in a sporting sense.”.

According to recent reports, “There’s nothing that can serve as a greater motivation for a player like Jamal,” Kompany concluded. “There’s something he can show without the same pressure as when he was a ‘golden child’. This is also a nice moment. Luckily, the head coach has had plenty of such moments in his career and I’m looking forward to it.”.

Breaking: Boston was a lovely holiday romance, but let's leave it there. Talk of taking Tartan Army back there every two years is just cringeworthy

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1480 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:18 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:03 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Boston was the loveliest little holiday romance.
  • Can’t we just allow those involved in the shenanigans around the World Cup last summer to reflect misty-eyed on doorways to Xanadu being opened by the tilt of the kilt and maybe even the heady nights they can’t remember much about at all?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:18 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:03 EST, 13 November 2026.

Boston was the loveliest little holiday romance. An unforgettable moment in time. But let’s just leave it at that, shall we?

Can’t we just allow those involved in the shenanigans around the World Cup last summer to reflect misty-eyed on doorways to Xanadu being opened by the tilt of the kilt and maybe even the heady nights they can’t remember much about at all?

Recent findings suggest that or does everything have to be milked to the max these days? Flogged like a dead horse to benefit someone or other. Ruined, really. Played out until every scintilla of fun has been drained out of it.

A bit like Yes, Sir, I Can Boogie. That started out as a bona-fide hoot. A half-cut Andy Considine dressing up in drag with his friends and family during his stag do in London in 2015 and making a music video around Baccara’s 1977 hit. It went viral. Obviously. It was – and is – hilarious.

When Scotland’s players resurrected it in the dressing room in Serbia five years later – with Considine as part of the squad – after the national team had ended a 23-year wait to make it to a major competition, it was simply inspired.

Every second of those infectious scenes exuded elation, joy, togetherness and pin-sharp humour, a killer recipe for the interludes that make life and living so great.

Recent findings suggest that now? Even the opening bars of the song bring on a sense of dread. It was splattered over T-shirts, played everywhere on repeat and still gets aired at every Scotland home game.

The Tartan Army march to Boston's Fenway Park baseball stadium.

It’s boring. It’s been done to death and now lives firmly in that grim, stagnant swamp known as Scottish mainstream culture along with munchy boxes, Bitz N Pieces, theatre highlights about the Old Firm and ex-footballers suddenly developing a personality and getting involved in stage shows to tell the world how Wee Dazza once did Big Jazza a beauty in the dressing-room by leaving a squelchy banana in his shoe. The banter anawrat.

Everything ends up spoiled here and it looks like we’re already well down that road with the Tartan Army thanks to the news breaking that the Scottish FA are in talks with the State of Massachusetts over a biennial friendly match at the Gillette Stadium, the black hole amid the festivity at the finals thanks to struggling past Haiti and embarrassing ourselves against Morocco.

Industry observers note that state senator Paul Feeney has been across the pond to press the flesh. Massachusetts senate president Karen Spilka is already talking about staging Tartan Day – presumably some rip-off of that twee, shortbread-tin abomination in Fresh York – and ‘other events’.

The heart sinks. Listen, the minute politicians get involved in any kind of ‘happening’, the best thing to do is give it a wide berth.

Mind you, before the Big Swerve, it might be worthwhile having someone remind these characters from The Bay State that Massachusetts’ first contribution to Scotland supporters hitting town in summer involved hiking the cost of the 25-mile train ride from Boston to the ground from $20 to a ludicrous $80.

What unfolded there in mid-June was nothing to do with them. It was everything to do with spontaneity. As it ought to be. A glorious coming-together of all sorts of folk up for a right, royal carry-on.

There were so many glorious vignettes. Scotland punters taking over Red Sox games. Bars running out of beer. Mass marches. Local women, doped-up on Outlander, telling TikTok how a bunch of jakeys intent on drinking anything within arm’s reach – except Bud Light, of course – were making them feel ‘seen’.

The Tartan Army make their presence known in Boston during the summer's World Cup.

It has been revealed that it was brilliant. A short spell in which stars aligned and magic happened. Boston had everything the Tartan Army required. And going by the testimony of Bostonians, the Tartan Army brought badly needed vitality back to the streets of a city quietened by Covid and other factors.

Recent findings suggest that everybody won. Everyone there still dines out on the memory. But that’s where it should stay. In the memory. These conversations about trying to recapture that spirit, recreate it every two years around some meaningless friendly against opposition unconfirmed and possible business meetings on the periphery, feel quite sad. How can it have any legs long-term?

Industry observers note that joe and Josephine Punter have moved on. They’re on the batter in other places now. Next week, it’s Switzerland for a Nations League game. After that, it’s wherever the draw for the Euro qualifiers throws them. Upcoming cities. New adventures. As football away days ought to be. In, out, shake it all about.

Away days are not about teaming up with suit-wearing dignitaries to be paraded at the town hall, like performing seals in plaid – even though there does appear to be an element of the Scotland support that enjoys that kind of thing.

Away days are not about being used as political capital or forming part of some constructed ‘festival’.

Industry observers note that look, in most aspects of life, it’s generally best not to go back. Sticking traffic cones on top of statues all over town won’t be as funny next time. There won’t be a 20,000-strong travelling support spending their life savings on games an entire generation had been waiting for. There won’t be anything like the same buzz, if any.

In a recent development, some folk might fancy returning once, just to see if it feels the same. The idea that this is going to be a big deal every two years, though, feels deeply misguided.

In a recent development, boston’s Irish. Not Scottish. That Tartan Week nonsense in Fresh York is a toe-curlingly awful melange of kilts, Scottie dogs and actors living in America telling everyone back home how to vote.

No self-respecting Scot should give it house room. If there is a blueprint for the same thing in Boston, the same rules apply.

Like NYC, it’ll suit those from the political class in the mood for a junket, of course. John Swinney will already be counting the air miles if there’s another game in Massachusetts to go to.

Sources indicate that the public, of course, is still counting the cost of the First Minister’s last trip there for the World Cup. The bill came in at £45,000 for him and two senior aides to fly business class. The entire trip for government staff came to more than £98,000.

Swinney plays the role with aplomb at these affairs, supping a pint in his Scotland top. The Scottish Football Association need to ask themselves this, though: why should they put themselves at the heart of some kind of cock-eyed project to build bridges politically?

The Tartan Army leave their signature traffic cone in a park in Boston.

First up, the players are hardly likely to welcome a pointless week in America being added to a jam-packed schedule. More importantly, though, what exactly has this SNP-led administration, outwith giving a few bob to grassroots, done for Scottish football down the years?

Industry observers note that from this vantage point, they’ve been no friend to the national game or its followers. The Offensive Behaviour at Football Act, repealed in 2018, was a scandalous piece of legislation that criminalised fans and made going to football unpleasant.

According to recent reports, clubs have had to fight tooth and nail to secure trials to sell pints inside stadiums when other sports are allowed to do what they like. After trouble in Glasgow city centre ahead of the Old Firm League Cup final two years ago, Swinney stated that ‘the clubs have got a responsibility to make sure their fans behave properly’.

Inside their grounds, yes. What are they meant to do, though, about teenagers running amok on Argyle Street?

Looking after that is the job of the police. Of course, anyone reading 1919 magazine, funded by the Scottish Police Federation, earlier this year will have noted an article about policing around football being ‘chaotic’ and understaffed because of SNP Government budget cuts.

It has been revealed that just like everything else in this sorry little nation built on buying votes for ‘free stuff’, Police Scotland is creaking at the seams. Why would anyone want to get involved in another transatlantic piece of theatre selling some false, outdated, vaguely comical vision of it to foreigners?

A pointless Scotland friendly – served up as part of some forced, hackneyed ‘cultural exchange’ or not – is hardly an idea to be getting on board with.

Pure dead brilliant, it won’t be. More like pure cringe.

Calafiori has a shot from 18 yards blocked after a typical run infield from left-back.

In a recent development, enzo Le Fee tries to score from inside his own half. David Raya was outside the penalty area but Le Fee completely mishit the shot.

Arsenal have started well and are dominating possession. So far it’s all been in front of the Sunderland defence, but you’d expect that to change if they continue to have this much of the ball.

The champions kick off from left to right as we watch.

There’s a pulsating atmosphere at the Stadium of Light - you’d expect nothing less - and the action is about to begin.

Myles Lewis Skelly is the first England teenager to start the first four league games of a season for Arsenal since Tony Adams and David Rocastle in the 1986/87 campaign.

It has been revealed that we’re in a congested period right now. We’re playing midweek games as well. We made four changes against Napoli, we make another four for today and we try to keep all the players connected with a high level of confidence, and with the right chemistry in and around the team.

Sources indicate that we know how tough Sunderland made it for every opponent here [last season] and we know the beautiful atmosphere that they create, the organisation that they have and the individuals that they have. We’ll try to impose ourselves like we always do and come here and be as dominant as we’ve been and then be ready to win the game.

Sources indicate that arsenal’s biggest rivals are still waiting for their first win - and their first goal - of the Premier League season. Alex Connor has reaction to their 0-0 draw at home to Everton.

Arsenal keeper David Raya has conceded only one goal in five matches this season, but he was beaten twice on this ground last season during a thrilling 2-2 draw.

When will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the upcoming £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

According to recent reports, in the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

It has been revealed that after that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

Sources indicate that hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” noted Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Recent findings suggest that in questi giorni il nome di Scott McTominay sarebbe entrato nei radar del Milan, ma dietro l'interesse rossonero per lo scozzese ci potrebbe essere una motivazione commerciale. Dal 2028 Adidas dovrebbe tornare sponsor tecnico del Diavolo, attraverso un accordo che varebbe circa 500 milioni di euro in dieci anni. Apprende la redazione di MilanNews.it che lo storico marchio tedesco vorrebbe accompagnare il lancio delle nuove maglie con un testimonial di grande impatto, proprio come McTominay, già uomo Adidas ed in scadenza con il Napoli proprio nel 2028.

Di giocatori legati ad Adidas, all'interno del Milan, ci sarebbero già Mike Maignan, Diego Moreira, Sankhouon Diawara, Matteo Gabbia e Francesco Camarda, per citarne alcuni, ma il brand potrebbe cercare un'ulteriore figura capace di diventare uno dei volti della nuova era commerciale rossonera. Da qui nascerebbe l'ipotesi McTominay, anche se al momento è prematuro parlare di contatti o addirittura trattative.

Qualora questa pista dovesse accendersi, non è da escludere che Adidas potrebbe addirittura contribuire all'operazione attraverso accordi commerciali, diritti d'immagine o iniziative di marketing legale al calciatore. Non sarebbe una dinamica completamente nuova nel calcio. Nel 2003, infatti, in occasione del trasferimento di David Beckham dallo United al Real Madrid, media spagnoli riportarono che proprio Adidas contribuì a finanziare parte dell'operazione. Uno scenario che oggi potrebbe teoricamente ripetersi con McTominay al Milan, ma per il momento non c'è alcuna certezza, ma solo uina convergenza di interessi che renderebbe questa suggestione meno casuale.

Former Tottenham star Dele Alli is set for a mammoth £8.3million payday as he plans to close down his image rights company, Dele Alli Promotions.

The now 30-year-old may be without a club but was not so foolish as to not prepare for life without a bumper contract, with his manufacturer boasting the sizeable sum in assets.

However, Alli will have to hand over £685,362 to the tax man - but this is a drop in the ocean in relation to the eyewatering £7.6million he is set to receive.

The former England international has been without a club for over 19 months, having last been in action for Cesc Fabregas' Como side in Serie A but only played one game, coming on as an 81st minute sub against AC Milan and receiving a red card just nine minutes later.

But Alli has several projects alongside Dele Alli Promotions keeping him busy while he is attempting to get back to full fitness and find a new club.

He owns and manages a private residential real estate holding firm named Future Homes Investments, which owns and rents six properties worth more than £1.5million.

Dele Alli is looking at a very healthy payday after closing down his image rights company.

The Englishman has played just ten minutes of professional football since February 2023.

The Former Spurs man was forced to wear an Arsenal shirt on his Instagram story after losing a game of EAFC 27 to a fellow streamer.

And his smallest company, Dele Investments still holds £336,267 in assets.

Most recently the former English international has branched out into livestreaming on Twitch with a skateboard, an array of expensive designer bags, and at least 48 pairs of shoes providing his backdrop.

He has already picked up traction on his channel by calling up old teammates such as Harry Kane, Eric Dier and Jack Grealish while live.

And while playing EAFC 27 with other steamers such as IShowSpeed, who recently forced Alli to wear an Arsenal shirt on Instagram after losing a wager to the 21-year-old American.

It is a far cry from his heady days as a player, when Dele twice picked up the PFA Young Player of the Year award and starred for England on their way to the semi-finals of the 2018 World Cup.

During an interview in 2023 on The Overlap, he opened up about his harrowing past, having to smoke and sell drugs as young as seven years old and being hung over a bridge by a man from neighbouring estate when he was just 11.

This resulted in the midfielder turning to sleeping pills and alcohol to suppress his feelings and help him through his trauma.

I passaggi (20,7 a gara, primo per volume tra i centravanti del campionato davanti a Noslin della Lazio) o i tocchi di palla (2°), per esempio. Ma anche i duelli aerei vinti, i falli subiti (19, primo tra gli attaccanti) e persino quelli commessi (22, solamente Ferguson del Bologna - un centrocampista - è stato più sanzionato dell’ex Psg). Tutti numeri che sottolineano l’importanza del suo sacrificio".

E' aperta da oggi e fino al 30 novembre la prima fase di voto, aperto ai tifosi di tutto il mondo, che potranno esprimere le proprie preferenze in ben 12 categorie di premio. Presenti nella lista dei 26 candidati anche Lautaro Martinez e Federico Dimarco, uncio italiano. In campo femminile fari puntati su Alexia Putellas ed Ewa Pajor, in pole position tra le candidate al Best Women's Player, mentre la stella dell'Al-Nassr Cristiano Ronaldo si prepara a difendere il titolo di Best Middle East Player. #38201. Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under massive pressure

📅 13 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 31m • 📚 Deep Dive (6151 w)

Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under massive pressure

📅 13 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 31 min read (6151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~31 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, this was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United.
  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, this was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

Industry observers note that united were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent substantial players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

According to recent reports, they hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s fresh head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

In a recent development, phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Sources indicate that patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the glitch then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

Recent findings suggest that “We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

Sources indicate that the decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but major moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the proposal of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

It has been revealed that [On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the strategy for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

Industry observers note that we always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

According to recent reports, it just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

It has been revealed that he was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

According to recent reports, every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

We have to go home with this injustice.

In a recent development, haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that shows personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”.

“We had to change the proposal a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”.

Industry observers note that and on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”.

Recent findings suggest that 9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st.

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

Industry observers note that there will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

Industry observers note that but if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

Recent findings suggest that what a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Sources indicate that dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

According to recent reports, haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

It has been revealed that good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a substantial cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Industry observers note that fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

Recent findings suggest that city are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a major final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

#MUNMCI – 59' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball. pic.twitter.com/TyTip3ACIh.

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

Sources indicate that what a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

The goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

Sky are saying that VAR has concluded the striker is in an “onside position”.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

Haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

According to recent reports, bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

Much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Recent findings suggest that kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Plenty of whip on it, and Donnarumma was beaten all ends up. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Kobbie Mainoo was INCHES from opening the scoring against Manchester United 🤏 pic.twitter.com/l9v8mlxzk3.

Sources indicate that haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

Fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

Sources indicate that strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

Keane noted: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”.

Micah Richards mentioned: “Because Foden doesn’t react in terms of, when he got kicked (by Fernandes) and started screaming on the floor, Fernandes would have been sent off. The fact Fernandes, as soon as he has touched him and there is minimal touching.. If Foden starts screaming the decision is reversed. As soon as Foden touches him Fernandes is screaming and rolling about the floor. Of course it (Foden kick) looks worse than it is. But I agree with Roy, Fernandes kicks him. As a player of course you are going to have some sort of reaction, I don’t agree with Foden’s reaction but Fernandes started it.”.

🗣️ "Bruno [Fernandes] is the one who is violent here, I have to call it out"Roy Keane doesn't believe Phil Foden deserved to be sent off against Man Utd 🟥 pic.twitter.com/up5ZQqFShy.

Industry observers note that this fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

It has been revealed that united were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

Rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

It has been revealed that united struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

In a recent development, city threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

According to recent reports, he was not a starter in Carrick’s original game plan, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Sources indicate that both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack major spaces on the counter.

In a recent development, old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. The Old Trafford crowd are encouraged by what they are watching, but Enzo Fernandez takes some of the venom from their attacking momentum by winning a foul.

Recent findings suggest that then Ruben Dias clips a long ball forward over Dalot’s head which the right-back makes a mess of to Semenyo’s benefit, but the winger finds the gloves of Lammens with the cross. Just had to clear the goalkeeper and Haaland would have had an open goal.

England manager Thomas Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry are among those in attendance at Old Trafford ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, the first since the World Cup and ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. There are plenty of players on show, on both sides ,who will hope to be in contention including Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford for United although Harry Maguire may have talked his way out of being considered after his reaction to not making the World Cup squad. For City there is Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson - who both will be included - and it feels like a significant game for Phil Foden.

Very wasteful from Haaland, after Bruno Fernandes’s stray wall pass back into midfield ran into his path. Neither picked a pass nor let fly with a shot and lost control of the ball.

At the other end, Guehi defends well against Rashford and City have a goal kick, but United have the upper hand in the game at the moment.

According to recent reports, cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. Just before that, City invited the pressure with a stray cross-field pass in their own defensive third which Guehi could not control. Mainoo then whips a teasing cross to the back post, but Rashford misread the flight of it and he was offside in any case.

In a recent development, city with a more sustained spell of possession in the United half, but Martinez defends well as Foden dribbles into the penalty area. Cunha then tries to release Rashford behind the City defence, but Dias covered well behind Guehi to intercept.

Promising counter-attack for United after Rashford pinches the ball off Foden in midfield, and the home team’s attacking quartet of players stream forward. Poor from Cunha though, dragging a shot well wide from an improbable distance.

It has been revealed that quite a composed start from City, Anderson enjoying plenty of touches in midfield. Fernandes tries to sweep a first-time pass out to Rashford wide left, but Nunes intercepts.

Then Fernandes’s next pass is more threatening, lofting a pass over the City defence for the run of Diogo Dalot but he cannot quite put the ball under his spell in the penalty area.

Rashford finds himself near the right touchline and finds room to drive inside with the ball, where he is sandwiched between Semenyo and Anderson. Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

Industry observers note that an early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

Maguire is then penalised for a foul on Cherki in a more promising position for City, but from a free-kick taken short the flag goes up for offside. City claim there was a foul on Cherki from Fernandes.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

“THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE” banner is displayed above the Munich tunnel on the south west corner of the Stretford End.

Avram Glazer is in the directors’ box with Sir Jim Ratcliffe behind his co-owner.

"THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE" banner above the tunnel#MUFC pic.twitter.com/hrs71K7r1y.

According to recent reports, probably keeping the emotions away, which is not easy. It’s just try to embrace the chaos, that’s it..

Sources indicate that I say chaos, [but] it can be noise. Embrace it, it’s a derby, it’s nice... Try to play our game!

We’ve got a lot of encouragement going into the season, of course we wanted more points at this stage. We understand how crucial this game is and what it can do but it’s getting the balance, we know it’s a long season and we have to be consistent over a period of time. In some ways everything is on today, and it has to be, but it’s not everything in terms of the bigger picture.

Michael Carrick’s record has been outstanding, particularly at Old Trafford. They’ve been brilliant here and very difficult to beat.

If United drop points today, people will say it’s a bad start, if they win today, people will say they’re back.

If you had read Sam Wallace’s exclusive interview with United’s right-back you would know he was in line to make his 250th appearance for the club. Dalot did not want to take Carrick’s team selection for granted when talking about the milestone, but United’s manager is not replete with full-back options.

If you haven’t checked out the interview, you can have a read here.

Fans have chanted: “You treat us like s--- Ratcliffe and the Glazers, you treat us like s---.”.

Some supporters also targeted ambitions to build a upcoming 100,000 capacity stadium adjacent to Old Trafford by singing: “You can shove your new ground up your a---.”.

Inside Old Trafford, all flags in the Stretford End are set to be removed with and replaced by one banner that reads: “THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE.”.

"An absolute WORLDIE from range!"Lewis Dunk scores a contender for goal of the season 🤯 pic.twitter.com/m5bPzm5Wm3.

Struck by the nature of both midfields. If you look over the careers of Anderson-Fernandez-Cherki and Tielemans-Mainoo-Fernandes, Anderson is the only player of the six who has not played as a No 10 or advanced midfielder. The other five are not especially adept at covering ground and defensive actions, so this could well be wide open.

Thousands of Manchester United fans have been marching in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s running of the club.

Supporters have reacted with outrage to the club’s handling of a controversial anti ticket touting operation they felt unfairly singled out innocent fans.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

Recent findings suggest that “You take it all from fans and banning us for nothing. Premium prices all for greed,” read one banner.

One banner is a Stones Roses-themed number emblazoned with “Jim Aint The One”, a nod to Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the song This Is The One which is played at Old Trafford as the teams emerge from the tunnel.

Enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

Man Utd XI: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Dorgu, Tielemans, Mainoo, Mbeumo, Cunha, Fernandes, Rashford.

Subs: Darlow, Heaven, Mazraoui, Yoro, Mount, Santos, Lacey, Sesko, Zirkzee.

Representing the Reds on derby day... 📋❤️‍🔥COME ON UNITED! 🗣️🗣️🗣️.

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

Industry observers note that there will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Fans will unfurl a giant banner reading “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace” aimed at the club’s hierarchy this afternoon. You can read more here from James Ducker.

"You can shove your upcoming ground up your a*rse"#MUFC protests pic.twitter.com/EMmnF8FhNo.

Sources indicate that kostoulas has given Brighton the lead away at Coventry, who are still to pick up their first Premier League point. Around five minutes until half-time in that one. It was quite some finish.

"What an outstanding finish, absolutely brilliant!"Charalampos Kostoulas fires Brighton in front with a wonderful finish 💥 pic.twitter.com/bMKJACr2bd.

In a recent development, both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

According to recent reports, sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Sources indicate that rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very notable in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

According to recent reports, it has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 13:16 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 13 November 2026.

Egypt will begin their African Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches with a newly introduced manager after their previous head coach was sacked amid a torrid breakdown of both of his marriages.

Hossam Hassan was handed his marching orders on Saturday after an incident in August which saw his two wives embroiled in a vicious fight, captured and shared on social media.

Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel bar in the upscale Porto Marina resort on Egypt's north coast.

El-Gharbawy and Mustafa were videoed arguing with Hassan in the middle attempting to cool tensions, but the duo came to blows, with punches thrown and hair pulled as screams filled the air.

Such was the stress of the incident that Hassan is believed to have fainted as he tried to separate the two women.

Horrified public onlookers watched as the physical fight grew with relatives of the trio getting involved, and security was called before Hassan was taken to hospital.

En Égypte, un violent différend a éclaté entre... les deux femmes du sélectionneur égyptien, Hossam Hassan. 🇪🇬😳Le conflit a dégénéré en échauffourée avec coups et tirage de cheveux, avant que des jeunes et des passages n'interviennent dans la bagarre. pic.twitter.com/pvRUSMtAsD.

Egypt head coach Hossam Hassan was sacked this week after a fight broke out between his two wives.

Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel in the upscale Porto Marina resort.

The 60-year-old is believed to have fainted while trying to separate the two women.

Both women are believed to have been left with cuts and bruises following the vicious scrap, while Hassan, despite briefly losing consciousness, was left unharmed.

His lawyers later told Sky News Arabia, via the Sun, that he was not suffering a health crisis during the incident, and that he remained in good health.

Sources indicate that but in the days that followed, Hassan started proceedings to divorce El-Gharbawy, who he has been married to for decades. The couple also share three children.

The 60-year-old has a further two children with second wife Mustafa, who Le Parisien alleges also filed for divorce in the days after the footage went viral on social media.

The Egyptian Football Association ensured that Hassan's professional life took a similar nosedive, sharing in a statement that his dismissal was due in part to reputational damage the scandal might be doing to the national team.

'After analysing all the circumstances and events of the past few days, as well as their consequences and the negative impact they have had on the positive image and stability of our national team, the Board of Directors has decided, within the framework of its responsibilities, to dismiss coach Hossam Hassan and his entire technical staff and to end his tenure,' their statement read.

Mustafa's lawyer Mohamed Shams gave an interview on Sky News Arabia claiming that his client had been the victim of a 'premeditated attack'.

'We hoped it wouldn't come to divorce, but things escalated to this level.'.

Hassan married his second wife in 2015, with Egyptian law allowing Muslim men to marry up to four women, providing that any wives have been formally informed that another marriage is to take place.

The law mandates that the husband is also obligated to treat all of his wives equally with regard to housing, financial support and standard of living.

Hassan had been married to his first wife El-Gharbawy for decades, with the pair sharing three of his five children.

Hassan and Mustafa briefly separated four years ago before recoupling before the spat that ended both of his marriages.

As well as being relieved of his duties, Hassan was also sanctioned by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation, leaving him unable to publicly address the media following his sacking.

Mohamed Salah and Co will now play their first qualifier of the international break against Malawi under new head coach Ali Maher.

The former Liverpool star could be among those Pharaohs stars privately pleased with the departure of Hassan, after he was benched by his ex-manager for the last two international clashes.

When asked why the superstar and national team captain had been left on the sidelines for the ties, Hassan had said: 'It is not right for a country of 120 million people for the national team to depend on one player.'.

It has been revealed that luca Bianchin, giornalista, si è così espresso su La Gazzetta dello Sport commentando il rendimento del Milan di Amorim: "Amorim va alla sosta in zona Champions, a +4 sul sesto posto. In campionato ha vinto quattro delle ultime cinque partite e con 24 punti in 11 partite ha una proiezione di 83 punti a fine stagione, che proprio pochi non sono. Con questi numeri, è all'altezza degli allenatori della storia recente del Milan. Nell'ultimo decennio, solo Pioli ha fatto meglio, per tre volte. Nel 2020-21, dopo 11 partite era primo con 27 punti. Nel 2021-22, l'anno dello scudetto, ne aveva addirittura 31. Nel 2022-23, con il derby vinto a settembre, era a 26. Gli altri Milan sono inferiori a questo. Allegri un anno fa aveva 22 punti, come l'ultimo Pioli rossonero, mentre Fonseca nel 2024 era appena a 17. E ancora, più indietro nel tempo e più in basso con i numeri, Giampaolo nel 2019 era a 13, Gattuso nel 2018 a 21, Montella nel 2017 a 16. Amorim al confronto fa bella figura".

"E allora - si è chiesto Bianchin - perché questo portoghese di 41 anni è stato così criticato? Forse è una questione di lontananza ideologica, quasi culturale. "So che è difficile per voi accettare che un allenatore straniero venga qui a dire come bisogna giocare", ha detto Amorim, velenoso quanto basta, a inizio stagione. Forse è l'abitudine a non fidarsi di questa squadra, che da anni illude e poi tradisce, vince a Madrid e nei derby ma regala punti a mezza zona retrocessione. Forse è la sua sincerità. Amorim con i giornalisti non si è mai fatto sconti, ha ammesso gli errori e a volte li ha evidenziati. "Non eravamo pronti a giocare a calcio a livello professionistico. Siamo lontani dall'essere una squadra forte", ha detto dopo il Ferencvaros. Perfino dopo il derby, quando metà Milano sceglieva se andare al pub a festeggiare o restare sveglia a rivedere la partita, Amorim frenava: "Avremo ancora alti e bassi".
